transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been having a little trouble keeping up with some things lately. It's probably normal, you know, just transitioning out of college and everything, but I keep sort of... misplacing my priorities, I guess? Like, I'll mean to pay a bill, or reply to an email about a job interview, and it just slips my mind. I've missed a couple of appointments, too, and forgotten to run errands that I promised I'd do. 

It's really embarrassing to admit, actually. I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or irresponsible. I really try to be on top of things! But it's just... it's started to cost me some real opportunities, and I want to make sure I'm doing everything right. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing people usually come to see you for?

When you say things slip your mind, does this happen pretty much everywhere — like at work, at home, when you're with friends — or is it mainly happening in certain situations, like when you're stressed about the transition?

Um, I guess it's kind of everywhere, unfortunately. I really wish I could say it was just the stress of the transition. I... well, I should probably be completely honest with you, even though it's really hard to admit. 

I actually don't have a job right now. I sort of... got let go recently. I feel terrible even saying that out loud, and I promise I'm normally a really hard worker! But since getting fired, I've just been messing up the next steps, too. Like, I've missed a few important interview follow-ups, and I even had to step back from a volunteer project that I really, really cared about because I just couldn't keep my commitments straight. 

So, yeah, I'm unemployed right now, and I just feel like I can't reliably manage the basic steps of moving my life forward. I'm sorry, is that too much information? Am I answering your question okay?

Looking back to when you were younger — say, in elementary school or high school — did you have similar kinds of trouble keeping track of things and remembering to do tasks, or is this something that's really only started happening more recently?

Um, well... I guess it’s not entirely new. I really hate admitting this, because I always wanted to be the perfect student, and I really did try my best! But, yeah... even back in elementary school, I had some of these same issues. 

My teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, which was really sweet of them, but... they'd also write that I was constantly losing my worksheets. Or that I’d rush through the directions and miss things. And I guess I talked out of turn a lot, too. I just got so eager to participate, you know? I really wasn't trying to be disruptive or disrespectful! 

And, um... my desk was always just a complete disaster. It was so messy that I literally couldn't find my assignments when it was time to hand them in. It’s so embarrassing to look back on, honestly. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was an awful kid. I promise I was a good kid, I just struggled to keep it all together! Does that help answer your question, or did you mean more recently?
When you were younger and even now, have people ever commented that you seem to be constantly on the go, fidgeting, or having trouble sitting still — like you have a lot of restless energy?

Um, yeah... I guess people have mentioned that. I really hope it doesn't make me sound frantic or, like, hyper or anything! I always just tried to frame it as being highly motivated, you know? 

But... well, to be completely honest with you, even without a job right now, I am just constantly moving from one thing to the next all day long. Like, I'll start the laundry, and then suddenly I'm checking my emails, and then I'm reorganizing all the tabs on my computer browser, or just pacing around my apartment, and then I'm starting to prep dinner... it's like I just physically cannot let myself stop moving. 

I know it probably sounds like a good thing to have all that energy, and I really do try to use it well! But the embarrassing part is that, even with all that running around, none of it actually gets finished. I just sort of bounce around leaving a trail of half-done tasks. 

Is that... is that what you mean by restless energy? I hope I'm explaining that right. Am I giving you the kind of examples you're looking for?

When did you first notice that you were having trouble sitting still and staying focused on tasks — was this something that was happening back in elementary school, or did it start at a different point in your life?

Um... well, the moving around constantly and, like, the really intense trouble finishing things? I know I mentioned I struggled a bit when I was a kid, but it really wasn't this bad back then. I promise I was mostly able to keep it under control! 

But, um... this level of it, where it's just completely taking over my life... I'd say that really started about, maybe a year and two months ago? I think that's right. It kind of started around the time things were getting really bad at the biotech job I had, right before I got let go. And it's just... it's just continued since then, even though I've really, really been trying to get a handle on it. I don't want you to think I haven't been trying! 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay, I just wanted to be clear that it hasn't always been this severe.

Around the time this worsening started — about 14 months ago when things were getting bad at your job — did anything else happen in your life? Like, did you have any head injuries, start taking any new medications, use any drugs or alcohol more heavily, or notice any changes in your physical health like sleep problems, appetite changes, or fevers?

Um, no, nothing like that! I promise I wasn't doing anything reckless or... or bad. I definitely didn't hit my head, and I'm not really a drinker or anything. I just take my normal vitamins, no new medications or anything like that. 

And physically, I've been totally fine! No fevers or, um, weird changes in my appetite or anything. I mean, my sleep is maybe a little scattered sometimes just because my mind is going, but I really try to get a good night's rest, I promise! 

I really don't think anything else was going on. I just... I think the stress of the job just kind of got to me, maybe? I hope that's an okay answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so you don't think there was some big, dramatic reason for it all!

When you were in elementary school and had trouble with your desk being messy and losing worksheets — was it as severe as what you're experiencing now, where you can't finish tasks and things are piling up? Or was it noticeably less intense back then?

Um... well, when I really think about it... I guess it actually was pretty noticeable back then, too. I always try to focus on the positive, so I mostly just remember that my teachers always wrote on my report cards that I was a really bright student! I always appreciated that they noticed that. 

But... um, to be completely honest with you, they also wrote that I rushed through directions a lot, and that I talked out of turn. I promise I was never trying to be a bad kid or be intentionally disruptive! I think I just got a little too eager sometimes, you know? 

And the desk thing... yeah, it was actually pretty bad. I was constantly losing my worksheets, and my desk would get so incredibly messy that I literally could not find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. It was always so embarrassing for me to have to admit I lost them. 

So... I guess maybe it actually *was* pretty intense back then, too? It just looked a little different because I was little and had teachers kind of structuring my day for me. I hope it's okay that I'm explaining it this way... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit. Does that help answer your question?
